title: Bot token accepted via command-line argument is exposed in process list and shell history
reasoning: The failure message instructs the user to pass the bot token as a positional CLI argument, and the __main__ block writes sys.argv[1] into TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. Credentials passed via argv are visible in ps/top output for the process lifetime, persist in shell history, and are echoed into CI logs and shell wrappers. The script already supports TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/BOT_TOKEN env vars plus .env and config.json fallbacks, so the argv path is an unnecessary credential-exposure vector. The argv value also mutates the process environment, so any child process inherits the secret.
reproduction: Run `python3 update_bot_button.py 1234567890:ABCD...` and observe the full token in `ps aux` output and in shell history; any CI step that echoes the command will also log the token.
recommendation: Remove the argv token path (lines 53-56) and the usage hint (line 35). Require the token via TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/BOT_TOKEN env vars or the existing .env/config.json fallbacks, or read it from stdin without echoing (e.g., getpass).
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature ships with no tests (tests: []), and the argv override is only exercised in ad-hoc manual runs.
suggestedRegressionTest: A unit test that monkeypatches os.environ and asserts get_token() prefers TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN over .env/config.json and that no token is accepted from sys.argv, so the argv path can be removed without regressing env-based resolution.
